name: Azaziah
overview: Azaziah was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim, known primarily as the father of Hoshea. His mention in Scripture is limited, with no additional personal details or notable events recorded beyond his paternal relationship. This brief record situates him within the genealogical and tribal context of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Azaziah means 'y-h-v-h is strong,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors the strength of the LORD. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:20, underscores a recognition of God's power inherent in his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Azaziah as a descendant of the tribe of Ephraim and the father of Hoshea. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Azaziah's significance lies chiefly in his role as the father of Hoshea, who is noted in the same passage, situating Azaziah within the tribal leadership or census of Ephraim. While not a prominent figure in the narrative, his mention contributes to the genealogical records that affirm God's providential care over the tribes of Israel and the continuity of His covenant people.
